title: The city that danced for weeks and nobody knows why
hook: A whole city danced for days, and nobody could stop it.
summary: In 1518 hundreds of people in Strasbourg danced for days without rest; the cause is still unknown.
sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Dancing plague of 1518, Strasbourg, began July 1518 with a woman, Frau Troffea; about 400 affected; cause unknown
Historian John Waller, 'A Time to Dance, A Time to Die' (2009): city records, physicians' notes, shrine of St Vitus at Saverne, theories of ergot and mass psychogenic illness

lines.text: It began in Strasbourg in July fifteen eighteen, with one woman named Troffea.
lines.caps: It began in *Strasbourg | in *1518, | with one *woman

lines.text: Within a month, about four hundred people had joined her.
lines.caps: Within a *month, | about *400 people | had *joined her

lines.text: Doctors found no illness, so officials ordered more music and dancing.
lines.caps: Doctors found *no illness, | so *officials ordered | more *music

lines.text: It made things worse. Some people reportedly collapsed from exhaustion.
So they sent the dancers to a shrine, and by September it ended.
lines.caps: So *they sent them | to a *shrine, | and by *September | it *ended

lines.text: Poisoned bread? Stress that spread? Nobody knows.
Five hundred years later, nobody knows why.

post.caption:
In 1518, hundreds danced in Strasbourg for days. Historians still argue about why.
What's your theory: poison or panic?
